claims.text: Local lattice distortions and nanoscale chemical short-range order govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions and chemical short-range order create heterogeneous nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
These structural and chemical heterogeneities cause a sharp, hysteretic first-order transition.
Reducing internal lattice strain and promoting modest grain coarsening while preserving the ordered hexagonal state will broaden the phase transformation and reduce its hysteresis.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have a single-phase ordered hexagonal structure.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films inherently contain nanoscale chemical short-range order and local lattice distortions.
A post-deposition annealing or substrate-temperature increase of 50–100 degrees Celsius can relax lattice strain and slightly coarsen the microstructure while preserving the ordered state.
The relevant structural mediator is the state of local lattice distortion and the distribution of chemically ordered clusters at grain boundaries and within grains.
Reducing internal strain and changing the distribution and size of short-range-ordered clusters minimizes abrupt local energy barriers.
Minimizing local energy barriers broadens the magnetostructural transition and reduces pinning of moving phase boundaries.
Reduced phase-boundary pinning decreases hysteresis, potentially at the cost of a lower peak entropy change.
Annealed or substrate-heated samples will have a broader magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed or substrate-heated samples will have a smaller hysteresis width than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed or substrate-heated samples will have a slightly lower but more reversible peak entropy change than the as-deposited baseline.
The predicted reduction in hysteresis and increase in reversibility will enhance overall low-field magnetic-refrigeration cycle efficiency.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloys exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with a large but hysteretic entropy change.
The predictions apply only within a processing window that relieves lattice strain without disordering or transforming the ordered hexagonal matrix.
The magnitude of the hysteresis and entropy-change response depends on grain growth, lattice-strain relaxation, composition, and processing conditions.
